    Every touchdown probability

    Every skill player gets a probability of at least one rushing or receiving touchdown, built from projected team points and each player's recent usage, snap share, depth-chart role and who is out. Tested on 2018-2025 games it beats simple usage rankings, but the edge is modest: the top-ranked player on a team scores about 41% of the time. A 25% chance means about one in four, not a pick. The market column is the average of FanDuel's and DraftKings' raw implied probabilities, where available.

    Most-used players and deep shots
    Deep shots

    Throws of 20 or more air yards, and throws into the end zone from outside the 20. These are shown as data and are not part of the touchdown picks below: in the Week 6 backtest, only 4 of 40 passing touchdowns came on deep throws, and adding them to the picks did not help.

    How the prediction is made

    Touchdown lists. Most likely = the two players per team with the highest model chance of a rushing or receiving touchdown, chosen by the model alone. Market = average implied probability across the books that list the player (vig not removed). The screenshots show about 15 players per game, so some favorites have no line. Gaps have not been graded yet.

    How to read this

    • n is how many plays, attempts or carries a number rests on. Italic means fewer than 30. The NFL column covers every team in the same situation.
    • The defense column describes plays run against that defense, so a pass share there is how often offenses passed against it.
    • Pass share counts every dropback: passes, sacks and QB scrambles. Carries are designed runs, so scrambles are counted separately. Penalty-nullified plays, kneel-downs and spikes are left out.
    • Injury report shows each team's latest published report. This week's reports are not out until practice reports begin, so this is the report for the previous game. "No designation" means listed with practice participation only. The files carry no timestamp and omit game-day inactives.
    • Pos is the roster position. Throws by position group use the receiver's roster position. No intended receiver is throwaways and similar attempts.
    • Not available yet: formations, personnel groupings, routes, coverage types and where players line up on each play. Those files are not published for 2026.
    • Data: play-by-play and EPA from nflverse (nflfastR); charting from FTN Data via nflverse, CC BY-SA 4.0. Times are Eastern.

    Rebuild in progressno predictions this week

    The matchups below show this season's stats only. Score predictions, touchdown chances, props and parlays are paused while the player sim is rebuilt.

    Why

    • Week 10 grade: the sim picked 8 of 14 winners; the betting favorite won 9.
    • Props the sim rated 60–70% likely hit 49% of the time.
    • When the sim disagreed with the sportsbook, the sportsbook was closer. So its "edges" were mistakes, not value.

    What is being rebuilt

    • How spread out each player's outcomes are (the sim was too sure of itself, especially on catches and receiving yards).
    • Who gets the work when a player is out, learned from past games instead of rules of thumb.
    • Quarterback rushing and passing volume, which ran high.
    • Weekly team strength updates, which stopped after Week 7.

    How it will be tested

    • Each fix is tuned on 2019–2022 and tested on 2023–2025 results, and kept only if it is clearly better.
    • Then it is checked against 2026 sportsbook closing prices from DraftKings and FanDuel, which none of the fixes were tuned on.
    • Predictions come back to this page only when the rebuilt sim is at least as accurate as the sportsbook.

    Stats run through Wednesday's Packers-Rams game (Week 12). Injury lists show the Week 12 reports posted so far; Sunday's teams get final reports on Friday. Touchdown picks and paper-money results: Paper money tab.

    Paper money trackertest picks, not recommendations

    Every game, each version logs two picks before kickoff: the player most likely to score, and the most likely excluding each team's lead running back. Each pick is an imaginary $10 bet at the best DraftKings/FanDuel price when logged. If a player is inactive, or gets hurt and the sportsbooks void his bets, the bet is void. A third pick, the model value pick, is for each model, the player it rates 25–40% with the biggest gap above his price. From Week 12 the main value pick uses a cooldown: a player who was that model's value pick in either of the last 2 weeks is skipped and the next-best edge is taken. The original version (no cooldown) is still tracked with paper money for comparison. Picks logged after kickoff don't count. This is how the rebuilt TD models get tested on games they have never seen.
